raw.assessment: The incumbent provides staffed key access, telephone/in-person booking and recurring access for eleven groups, but leaves one group underserved. Observed administration averages 127.5 minutes weekly, above the 120-minute target; three conflicts occurred in four weeks. Neither the 90% needs target nor eight-week performance is established. Aggregate spare capacity does not establish usable availability: H4-O5 supplies a concrete limiting observation, since only one room has a piano and blank equipment fields cannot establish interchangeability. Evening concentration is another plausible restriction. Late or missed sessions suggest possible lost use, but their causes and recoverability are unknown.

openings.claim: Can reassignment within recorded acceptable windows meet needs, or does compatible demand exceed particular room/time capacity?
openings.delta: Replace aggregate utilization as the diagnostic with an explicit feasibility check that distinguishes missing coordination from localized scarcity.
openings.prediction: A feasible allocation after documenting windows and equipment would support the coordination account; an unavoidable overlap among piano-dependent or narrow-window needs would identify a capacity bottleneck despite unused room-hours elsewhere.
openings.probe: Use short contact conversations to record weekly rehearsal duration, acceptable windows and necessary equipment. Map an eight-week candidate allocation using existing rooms/hours, protecting both performances and every requested weekly 60-minute entitlement before allocating additional time. Report unmet needs explicitly; count offsite rehearsals only as context, not building provision.
assumptions: Contacts can describe their groups' needs accurately.
A feasible allocation is a hypothesis, not an established outcome.

openings.claim: One authoritative reservation ledger with confirmation identifiers may reduce conflicting expectations and duplicate calendar work.
openings.delta: Make each reservation/change effective only when entered and confirmed against the desk-accessible ledger; label the online copy with its update time.
openings.prediction: Calendar disagreement conflicts should decline; conflicts despite matching confirmations would indicate another cause. Total administration may fall or rise.
openings.probe: For eight weeks accept calls and desk requests, confirm room/time and superseded entries, and check keys against the ledger. Record conflicts, all groups' fulfilled needs, and total weekly administration, including confirmation and copying work.
assumptions: The volunteer and staffed desk can consult the authoritative record before confirming changes.
The two unexplained double arrivals need not share the calendar-disagreement cause.

raw.assessment: Unused reserved time, concentrated requests, unknown equipment needs and inconsistent records leave several plausible explanations for unmet needs. Existing observations do not establish that usable capacity is sufficient. Feasibility and administration cost must be checked against all eight-week targets.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: replacing inherited repeating times with assignments based on stated acceptable windows, required duration and equipment can meet more rehearsal needs within existing capacity.
openings.delta: Contact each group briefly by telephone or in person, record its actual needs, and construct a proposed eight-week schedule. Protect the two performances and each requesting group's weekly 60-minute minimum before distributing remaining time; count that minimum as full satisfaction only when it meets the group's stated need.
openings.prediction: If inherited assignments cause avoidable exclusion, the proposed schedule will satisfy more stated needs than the current schedule using the same rooms, equipment and staffed hours. If acceptable windows and equipment requirements remain incompatible, reassignment alone will fail.
openings.probe: Compare current and proposed schedules against the same recorded needs, including piano requirements and protected events. Check every weekly minimum before implementation; then measure fulfilled needs, conflicts and total administration across eight weeks.
assumptions: Groups can state usable windows and duration needs.
Enough mutually compatible capacity exists for a feasible schedule; this remains unverified.
Groups will accept changed times within their stated windows.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: recording each reservation or change once in an authoritative desk ledger, then confirming its room, date and time to the group, will reduce conflicting expectations.
openings.delta: Continue telephone and in-person requests. Give bookings identifiers; record changes against those identifiers, confirm by read-back, and update the online copy from the ledger. Key handover uses the ledger. Treat this as a proposed workflow, not an established explanation of every conflict.
openings.prediction: Calendar disagreements and differing booking expectations should decline; administration could improve through fewer corrections or worsen through confirmation work.
openings.probe: During eight weeks, tally disagreements, access conflicts, correction time and all administration minutes, including setup. Inspect whether each conflict originated in inconsistent records or had another cause. Require fewer than two conflicts and an administration average of at most 120 minutes weekly while retaining minimum slots and performances.
assumptions: Desk staff and the volunteer can consistently consult the same ledger.
Confirmation effort fits the administration budget; this requires measurement.

openings.claim: Needs-based reassignment may remove inherited exclusion; compatible room/time demand may instead exceed capacity.
openings.discriminator: Compare current and proposed schedules against identical stated needs; unavoidable piano or narrow-window overlaps indicate localized scarcity despite aggregate vacancy.
openings.fit: preserves, conditional on feasible weekly minima
openings.probe: Briefly interview contacts for duration, acceptable windows and equipment; map eight weeks, protecting performances and requested weekly 60-minute minima before extras. Report unmet needs; minima satisfy full needs only when sufficient. Treat offsite rehearsals as context, not building provision.
openings.uncertainty: Contact accuracy, compatible capacity and acceptance of changed times remain unverified; lateness causes and recoverability are unknown.

openings.claim: One authoritative desk ledger plus booking identifiers and confirmations may reduce record disagreement, conflicting expectations and duplicate work.
openings.discriminator: Separate inconsistent-record conflicts from conflicts despite matching confirmations; administration may improve or worsen.
openings.fit: preserves, conditional on desk/volunteer shared access
openings.probe: Enter reservations/changes once; link and supersede changed entries, confirm room/date/time by read-back, timestamp the online copy and check keys against the ledger. Across eight weeks tally conflicts, causes, fulfilled needs and all administration, including setup, confirmations, copying and corrections.
openings.uncertainty: Two double arrivals lack established causes; consistent consultation and affordable confirmation effort require testing.

lineage.reason: Retains reassignment mechanism and baseline comparison.
Retains authoritative confirmations and copy timestamp.
Retains read-back, change lineage and setup costs.

post_distill.decision: Test feasibility before reassignment; trial the ledger. Preserve two rooms, 24 staffed hours, existing equipment, no new fees, telephone/in-person changes, weekly entitlements and both performances. Eight-week success remains unproved: require >=90% stated needs met within acceptable windows, <2 conflicts and <=120 administration minutes/week on average.
